text: Master Hobb spits slag-dust into the quench trough and squints with his one good eye. 'If the edge is rolled, lay it on the horn. If you came to haggle over coal prices, keep walking.'

choices.label: Ask why his anvil is running cold.
Slip two silver for his private iron rack.

text: Hobb wipes pig's blood and soot off a pair of tongs as salt wind rattles the shutters. 'Coastal brine pits honest steel in a fortnight. Bring your plate before the rivets seize.'

choices.label: Ask what steel works against sea-raiders.
Check the private rack we arranged earlier.

text: Hobb tests a glowing billet with a notched ball-peen hammer. 'Four provinces of dents hammered flat, and now we're forging beside an open volcano. Speak fast before the iron cools.'

choices.label: Commission heavy plate for the final breach.
Ask who still owes him for militia pikes.

text: 'The capital sent wagons of peacock plumes instead of pig-iron, and bog-water rotted my last birch charcoal. Bring salvaged blades if you want proper tempering.'

choices.label: Promise to clear the quarry supply road.

text: 'Keep your voice down—Garrick thinks these billets belong to the garrison. Pay coin upfront and you get spring-steel that won't snap on the first parry.'
'Gnolls and sand-raiders beat stolen plowshares flat; Dread Knights wear meteor-slag bolted to their collarbones. Aim for the joints, not the breastplate.'

choices.label: Ask where the contraband ore is coming from.

text: 'You kept your mouth shut and paid in real silver. Take the quenched blades off the back hooks—every fuller ground true by hand.'
'Talk doesn't heat a bloomery, commander, but if you actually open that iron road, my best rivets go on your shields first.'
'Quartermaster Tarn shorted my coal deliveries for two winters before he bolted. I keep his unpaid tallies nailed beside my bellows so I never forget.'
'Then let's temper something worth burying kings in. When the ash settles, at least our steel won't be the thing that broke.'
Widow Marta stirs a jar of fat black leeches with one walnut-stained finger. 'Don't touch the green bottles unless you want your gums bleeding before supper.'

choices.label: Ask about the marsh-fever spreading in camp.
Pay extra for her locked apothecary chest.

text: Marta ties a rue-soaked rag around her nose against the harbor stench. 'Saltwater turns a clean arrow-nick into green gangrene by nightfall. Buy your poultices now.'

choices.label: Ask what poisons the coastal covens use.
Request the private tinctures we discussed.

text: Marta grinds dried willow-bark in a stone mortar while grey ash sifts onto her apron. 'Sulfur smoke blisters lungs faster than blades. Drink bitter-root before you climb.'

choices.label: Stock up on draughts for the final assault.
Ask why she never returned to the capital.

text: 'Garrick wants heroic elixirs, and I have boiled turpentine, sheep fat, and three bruised roots. Bring me intact spore-sacs or viper glands if you want real medicine.'

choices.label: Pledge to secure the fen herb-trails.

text: 'Quiet—these vials aren't for the levy. Distilled nightshade and concentrated antivenom: one drop clears a fever, two drops stop a heart.'
'Hedge-hexers grease their barbs with corpse-tallow and mycotoxins. Plug your nostrils with rue before stepping into any sunken chapel or willow hollow.'

choices.label: Ask who taught them those recipes.

text: 'You don't waste my bottles on drunken brawls. Here—freshly decanted red-cap moss draughts, corked in waxed bladder-skin.'
'Words won't grow willow-bark in alkaline mud, but if you clear those paths, I'll brew your vanguard's antitoxins at half coin.'
'During the first border famine, rations were weighed in bone-dust. Everyone who survived owes a debt to someone who didn't make spring.'
'Take every bottle on the shelf. If the world burns down tonight, I won't need laudanum tomorrow.'
Sergeant-at-Arms Garrick taps his splinted forearm against a sheaf of mud-stained muster rolls. 'Sign your mark or clear the parade ground. I'm short forty pikes.'

choices.label: Ask about garrison morale and desertions.
Offer silver to inspect confiscated levy gear.

text: Garrick squints into the sea drizzle from beneath a dented basinet. 'My border lads hate ships almost as much as they hate salt pork. Keep them in tight shield-walls.'

choices.label: Ask for his tactical read on the coastal forts.
Draw from the reserve armory we arranged.

text: Garrick wipes grey soot off his muster slate. 'Half the names on this board are crossed out in red charcoal, commander. Point us at the last gate so we can finish the roll.'

choices.label: Commit the surviving borderers to the breach.
Ask about the men lost along the border.

text: 'Promissory notes don't stop gnoll cleavers. Half my watchmen are marching in leaky boots because the pay-wagons vanished between here and Ashbrook.'

choices.label: Promise to reopen the northern supply road.

text: 'Keep this off the quartermaster's slate. Deserters left behind decent ash-shaft quarrels and oiled brigandines—better in your hands than rotting in the cellar.'
'Never split a column in a narrow pass unless you hold both ridges first, and never trust an unguarded bridge at dusk. Someone inside the border opened our gates.'

choices.label: Ask who betrayed the border watch.

text: 'You keep my militiamen breathing when other captains use them as arrow-fodder. Take the veteran pickets from the inner barracks.'
'Good. Open that supply track and I'll have every able-bodied pikeman in the parish drilling before cockcrow.'
'Thirty years on the border teaches you one ledger rule: the crown collects taxes in silver, and the frontier pays the interest in farmboys' ribs.'
'Shields locked, pikes level. Let's clear the road so the survivors can finally go home.'
Old Fenwick leans on a twelve-foot ash punt-pole shod with a crooked iron hook. 'Two copper to cross alive, one copper if I just fish your boots out of the weir.'

choices.label: Pay double toll to see his river-salvage sack.

text: Fenwick spits into the grey harbor chop, wrapped in his stitched horsehide coat. 'Too much salt in this water for an honest river-rat, though drowned knights still wear shiny rings.'

choices.label: Ask about hidden coves and tidal channels.
Check what your hook dredged up for me.

text: Fenwick eyes the sluggish magma moat with professional disgust. 'Not a drop of water worth poling a punt across. Still, a ferryman knows how to read currents—even hot ones.'

choices.label: Ask him to guide the supply barges across.
Ask about the tolls people never paid.

text: 'Eel-traps are full of bloated horses, splintered barrels, and dead tax-clerks. Nobody's shipping honest timber while raiders hold the gravel bars.'

choices.label: Promise to clear the river crossings.

text: 'Keep your lantern low. Pulled these off a courier-barge before the crows found it—waterproofed cases, tarnished signets, and boots that still fit.'
'Don't follow green lights in the peat—that's dead bailiffs auditing frogs. Stick to gravel shelves where reeds grow short and stiff.'

choices.label: Ask what he smuggled before the war.

text: 'You pay the ferryman upfront without whining about the mud. Here—pick first from tonight's eel-weir haul before the guards sniff around.'
'Clear the gnolls off the gravel bars and I'll pole your wounded across free of charge—dry-shod, mostly.'
'Everyone thinks the river washes debts clean. Truth is, silt preserves everything—coins, bones, and the names of fools who shorted the boatman.'
'One last crossing, then. Keep your balance low in the boat and don't drop your shield over the gunwale.'
Quartermaster Bram adjusts spectacles with one cracked green lens and taps a scale-viper ledger. 'Water is four silver a gill, shade is two silver an hour, complaints are free.'

choices.label: Ask why caravan prices are so steep.
Grease his palm for black-market desert gear.

text: Bram fans his sun-blistered scalp with an invoice sheet as sea fog rolls in. 'Finally, air you don't have to chew. Now let's talk salvage margins on those sunken galleys.'

choices.label: Open the private account we set up.

text: Bram weighs obsidian slag on his brass balance-scale. 'Every war ends in an audit, commander. Make sure we hold the vaults when the counting starts.'

choices.label: Secure full quartermaster backing for the siege.
Ask who profited from the Redmarsh ambushes.

text: 'Three mule-trains vanished in the Twin Passes, and salt-glare ruins leather straps in a week. Bring intact horn-bows or quarry ore if you want fair trade.'

choices.label: Pledge to secure the canyon caravan routes.

text: 'Off the imperial manifest: scale-viper bracers, curved desert steel, and rings stripped from nomad chieftains. Coin upfront, no receipts.'
'Whoever armed the Sand-Clans used Deep Quarry ironstone stamped with Border Mint dies. Follow the coin, not the war-horns.'

choices.label: Ask who signed those mint manifests.

text: 'A commander who understands overhead is rare. Take the prime stock from the locked chest—discounted for prompt settlement.'
'Open the pass and my wagons roll at dawn. Clean margins for me, fresh bolts for your archers.'
'In the Redmarsh, unpaid debts turn to salt-crust. Every merchant out here insures his wagons twice—once with guards, once with raiders.'
'The ledger is balanced and the war-chest is open. Take what you need to close the account.'
Chronicler Zahra holds up a lapis-stained hand before your boots touch her papyrus rolls. 'Wipe the alkali mud off your greaves; this inscription is older than your kingdom.'

choices.label: Ask what the desert ruins reveal.
Fund her private excavation with silver.

text: Zahra polishes a quartz magnifying lens against her indigo linen sleeve. 'First-Empire seawalls align with the Redmarsh wardstones. Whoever built them was measuring the caldera.'

choices.label: Ask how the coastal runes connect to the south.
Review the decoded tablets I funded.

text: Zahra traces obsidian glyphs with trembling blue fingertips. 'We are standing inside the lock mechanism of the continent, commander. Do not break a seal you haven't read.'

choices.label: Commit to preserving the Threshold archives.
Ask about the true origin of the Crown of Order.

text: 'Damp rot and blood-chanters are destroying pre-dynastic steles faster than I can press charcoal rubbings. Protect my surveyors if you want their wards deciphered.'

choices.label: Promise to safeguard her field rubbings.

text: 'These quartz focuses and pre-imperial scrolls were salvaged from sunken observatories. Keep them out of the quartermaster's crate—he'd melt the brass fittings.'
'The wardstones were never weather-charms—they are nails pinning subterranean pressure down. Crack enough of them and the whole basin wakes up.'

choices.label: Ask who forged the original seals.

text: 'Scholarly patronage is rare in a war camp. Take these translated ward-scrolls—they'll blunt any hex the coven throws at you.'
'Bring me intact boundary rubbings and I will map every blind spot in their ancient fortifications.'
'History in Thornvael is written on tomb-liens and tax-slates. Even the First Emperors bound their wardens in eternal servitude rather than pay a pension.'
'The glyphs are clear at last. Step onto the dais with open eyes, and choose what future survives.'
Cask-Master Tull taps the brass spigot strapped to his back-barrel with a wooden ladle. 'Don't ask where the well is—just ask if I boiled the scorpions out first.'

choices.label: Ask about water rations for the march.
Pay extra for a sealed skin of sweet-water.

text: Tull stares at the pouring coastal rain with tears cutting tracks through desert dust on his cheeks. 'Free water falling right out of the sky... bad for business, great for kidneys.'

choices.label: Ask how the coastal cisterns are holding up.
Tap the private reserve cask we arranged.

text: Tull wraps wet wool around his brass spigot to keep sulfur ash out of the nozzle. 'Out here a man sweats out his memories before noon. Keep your canteens capped.'

choices.label: Ensure clean water reaches the siege lines.
Ask about the wells poisoned during the drought.

text: 'Alkali dust turns clear water to chalk in an hour, and Lantern Eels fouled my main cistern. Clear the wells if you want your vanguard marching upright.'

choices.label: Promise to cleanse the Redmarsh cisterns.

text: 'Kept this cask buried in cool clay under my cot—unboiled mountain snowmelt, mixed with mint and iron-tonic. Worth more than crown gold.'
'Follow the pack-lizards at dusk—they smell sweet-water beneath dry creek beds. And never trust a oasis guarded by silent vipers.'

choices.label: Ask why Gorrathul dammed the mountain aquifer.

text: 'You didn't try to commandeer my barrels at sword-point. Dip your ladle deep—best heat-ward elixirs in the basin.'
'Save the sweet-water wells and I'll keep your company's canteens full at half tariff all the way to the mountains.'
'In a drought, every cup of water carries someone else's thirst on its rim. Plenty of ghosts in Redmarsh still waiting for a drink.'
'Last skins passed out, commander. Finish this war so we can all drink from an open river again.'
Chief Healer Sera wipes a blood-crusted bone saw on her oilskin apron. 'If you can walk into my tent unassisted, you aren't dying fast enough to skip the queue.'

choices.label: Ask about wounded overflowing the triage tents.
Offer silver for surgical-grade field kits.

text: Sera smells sharply of boiled vinegar and carbolic as coastal drizzle drums on the canvas roof. 'Saltwater festers shrapnel wounds in hours. Keep your bandages dry.'

choices.label: Ask what hazards await along the sea-cliffs.
Request the private medical chest we discussed.

text: Sera bandages a scorched forearm with grim efficiency. 'I've sewn men back together across three provinces only to watch them march into a volcano. Keep your shields up.'

choices.label: Commit full triage support for the final push.
Ask why she left the royal medical college.

text: 'I'm out of boiled linen, willow-bark laudanum, and clean sutures, while raiders harry my ambulance wagons on the shingle trails.'

choices.label: Promise to protect her field infirmaries.

text: 'These resurrection tomes and concentrated poppy-iron draughts came from my own college trunk. Use them on veterans worth saving.'
'Cinder Wards blister lungs from half a league off, and grave-runoff in the Sunken Citadel turns minor crab-nips lethal. Carry wet wool rags.'

choices.label: Ask what happens to those she cannot save.

text: 'You held the perimeter when my surgeons couldn't even lift a spear. Take our strongest restoratives—no coin needed today.'
'Guard the litters until we reach stone walls, and every man in my tent will live to swing a blade for you again.'
'The capital's royal college wanted surgeons to patch dukes' gout while borderers bled out in ditches. I kept my saw and burned my diploma.'
'My triage tables are set behind the basalt ridge. Bring your wounded back breathing, and I'll do the rest.'
Iron-Wright Kors hefts a heavy caulking mallet, tarred hemp braided into his beard. 'Armor's just a hull for a man's guts—keep the seams caulked or sink.'

choices.label: Ask why the drydocks are sitting idle.
Slip silver for marine-grade hull plate.

text: Kors squints out at the burning harbor channel, bronze rivets clinking around his neck. 'Six generations of shipwright craft reduced to floating charcoal. Help me clear the mole.'

choices.label: Ask how to breach Vesperion's blockade.
Inspect the reinforced shields we arranged.

text: Kors tests a basalt parapet with his caulking mallet. 'Give me oak planks over volcanic rock any day—at least wood groans before it splits.'

choices.label: Order siege-ram bracing for the Citadel gates.
Ask about the flagship he built for Kael.

text: 'No ironbark timber, no tarred oakum, and privateers blockading the channel. Until the mudflats clear, not a single troop barge touches salt water.'

choices.label: Promise to secure timber and oakum.

text: 'Forged these tower shields from salvaged keel-strakes and copper sheathing—sheds fire-arrows and turns aside boarding axes.'
'Kael's flagship is sheeted in copper against fire-pots. Don't waste pitch—reclaim the seawall culverins and smash her rudder-chains.'

choices.label: Ask how he knows her hull design so well.

text: 'You saved my shipwrights from the fire-ships. My yard hammers for your vanguard free of labor charges.'
'Bring me dry ironbark and oakum, and I'll have twelve seaworthy carracks caulked before the spring tide turns.'
'Every shipwright on the Iron Coast has built hulls for smugglers or tyrants to keep his apprentices fed. This crossing settles my ledger.'
'The transport fleet is anchored and your rams are iron-shod. Break their gates so we can sail home.'
Gate Warden Lyra rests a windlass arbalest across her bruised cheekbone. 'Wind's twelve knots sou'west—aim two fingers left of the breastplate if you want the throat.'

choices.label: Pay coin for custom-fletched steel quarrels.

text: Lyra checks the walnut stock of her arbalest against the sea fog. 'The council bolts its doors while my pickets run out of bowstrings. Ready to clear the cliffs?'

choices.label: Ask about enemy sniper positions ahead.
Collect the windlass gear we arranged.

text: Lyra squints through volcanic ash, adjusting her arbalest sights. 'Thermal updrafts bend long shots by a hand's breadth out here. Tell your archers to aim low.'

choices.label: Deploy her coastal marksmen for the final siege.
Ask about the traitor inside Oakhaven's council.

text: 'Half my watchmen are down to throwing roof-slates because Baron Vane hoarded the city's crossbow strings. We need seasoned yew and steel prods.'

choices.label: Promise to break the coastal supply blockade.

text: 'Keep these out of the council's sight—hardened steel-tipped quarrels and oiled stalker cowls from my personal watch-locker.'
'Sundered Ranks has interlocking fields of fire across the middle road, and floating Frost Bells freeze bowstrings along the riverlock. Hit the flanks first.'

choices.label: Ask who leaked Oakhaven's harbor charts.

text: 'You pulled my pickets out of the gatehouse when we had fourteen bolts left. My archers' quiver is yours.'
'Open the coast road and my best scouts will range ahead of your vanguard every mile to the straits.'
'Velvet tapestries for the baron, clipped tin wages for the men who died on the parapets. Someone always pays when cowards hold the keys.'
'Windlass spanned, sightlines clear. Give the signal and we'll pin their gunners to the obsidian.'
Mudlark Pip hoists a canvas sack dripping black harbor silt and grins with a missing front tooth. 'Found a dead knight at low tide! Couldn't get his boots off, so I took his ring.'

choices.label: Ask what washes up on the mudflats.
Slip him silver for his secret curio sack.

text: Pip shivers inside three oversized wool vests, swinging a bent iron crab-hook. 'Tide's going out fast by the sunken walls, boss—good time for pockets, bad time for heavy armor.'

choices.label: Ask about secret grates and back alleys.
See what shiny trinkets you hid for me.

text: Pip rubs grey caldera soot onto his nose like war-paint. 'No crabs out here, boss, just hot rocks—but dead knights still drop plenty of rings!'

choices.label: Hire him as a scout-runner for the siege.
Ask what happened to his mate Tommy.

text: 'Soldiers kick mudlarks for luck, then wonder why nobody tells 'em where the paymaster's strongboxes sank. Bring bread and copper if you want eyes in the silt.'

choices.label: Promise to split salvage fairly with him.

text: 'Don't tell Warden Lyra where these came from—found 'em wedged under the baron's sewer grate. Genuine silver signets and a charm that hums in the dark.'
'Stay clear of the Night Orchards after dusk—the skulls in the branches whisper your mum's name. Stick to the low-tide shingle instead.'

choices.label: Ask how he survives the harbor streets.

text: 'You actually paid half like you promised! Here—pick the best ring from my lucky tin before the big lads see.'
'Fair split, no kicks? Deal! I'll show you every blind culvert between the docks and the baron's keep.'
'Everyone in Oakhaven owes the sea something—a boat, a brother, or a boot. Best take what floats before the crabs get it.'
'Got my crab-hook and my lucky granite pebble, boss. Point out the narrow cracks and I'll slip right through.'
Captain Rowan adjusts the iron neck-brace bolted to his gorget, his scarred brow completely hairless. 'Don't salute out here—ridge snipers shoot anyone stupid enough to raise an arm.'

choices.label: Ask how Greystone Bastion is holding.
Offer coin for access to Ironcamp's reserve armory.

text: Rowan studies a soot-stained tactical map weighted down with basalt pebbles. 'Every yard between here and the Threshold is wired with traps and murder-holes.'

choices.label: Ask for his assessment of the Gauntlet.
Draw from the elite reserve we arranged.

text: Rowan rests a fire-blackened kite shield against his knee. 'We stacked our own dead in the breaches to hold this pass, commander. Don't waste what they bought us.'

choices.label: Unite all Ironcamp veterans for the Threshold.
Ask what High Command ordered behind his back.

text: 'Water tastes like boiled nails, sulfur eats leather straps in days, and demonic catapults are pounding my east parapet to gravel.'

choices.label: Promise to relieve the besieged walls.

text: 'These meteor-plated halberds and dread helms came off the citadel's own vanguard. My quartermaster doesn't log them—put them on your best men.'
'The Gauntlet is thirty paces wide between magnetic iron cliffs—archers miss, plate drags, and golems guard every portcullis. Bring grounding spikes and mauls.'

choices.label: Ask why the empire abandoned his garrison.

text: 'You held the wall when the mortars fell. My halberdiers march at your shoulder—no hiring fee.'
'Break their siege batteries and my veterans will hold your rear flank all the way to the Obsidian Dais.'
'High Command wanted the pass sealed behind us—left us here as a cork in a volcano. Only debt I honor now is to the men still breathing.'
'Banners furled, shields locked. Let's end this campaign so no soldier ever has to march into ash again.'
Forgemaster Vok peers through smoked-glass eye slits, four-foot tongs resting beside an open floor-fissure. 'No coal needed here—stick the billet in the crack and pull it out fast.'

choices.label: Ask why standard steel fails in the caldera.

text: Vok wipes silvery burn-keloids on his forearm with an asbestos rag. 'Normal iron turns soft as tallow near the vents. Bring me Anvilmaw jaws or prism-sand.'

choices.label: Ask how to crack Ashkarath's armor.
Commission the masterwork pieces we arranged.

text: Vok tests a white-hot maul-head with a spit-hiss. 'A thousand years ago my clan forged that glass throne under blood-contract. Time to see if our hammers can unmake it.'

choices.label: Have Vok re-temper the entire vanguard's gear.
Ask about his clan's ancient blood-contract.

text: 'My steam-hammer cracked its bedplate, and terrestrial ore melts like butter here. Hunt Anvilmaw Smiths if you want jaws hard enough to forge endgame plate.'
'Quenched these in brine and meteoric slag when Rowan wasn't looking—Gothic plate and obsidian mauls that laugh at hellfire.'
'Ashkarath's armor isn't buckled—it's bolted straight into his collarbone. Don't waste swings on his chest; strike the glowing seams where magma leaks.'
'Good ore deserves a proper smith. My fissure-hearth is yours—half price on every temper and reforge.'
'Drag those living anvils back on chains and I'll forge your company blades that stay keen until the world cools.'
'My ancestors poured the iron for the Obsidian Throne to buy peace for our deep halls. Worst bargain any smith ever struck.'
'Edges quenched, rivets locked, shields brined. Go strike the anvil inside that throne room.'
Brother Elias turns ash-caked bandages toward your footsteps, a brass thurible smoking in his hand. 'I see no heraldry, only the heat of your blood and the iron you bear.'

choices.label: Ask why he wears the penitent's collar.
Offer alms to study his charred scrolls.

text: Elias speaks in a voice like two pieces of pumice rubbing together. 'I looked directly at the Shattered Beacons when they lit. Now only the leylines burn beneath my soles.'

choices.label: Ask about the twin doors of the Threshold.
Consult the forbidden codices we discussed.

text: Elias fingers a bundle of charred vellum cylinders. 'Malrik feared growing old in a cold tower, so he sold the realm's spring. Soon you must choose which temperature remains.'

choices.label: Ask for his blessing before the Threshold.
Ask about his years teaching at the Ember Court.

text: 'Four cylinders of my old pyromantic syllabus still lie in the ruined scriptorium. Burn them before another fool uses my theorems to widen the breach.'

choices.label: Promise to recover and burn his syllabus.

text: 'These prismatic charms and astral tomes survived the beacon-fire. They steady the mind when the caldera whispers promises of power.'
'In the Threshold Chamber, the ancient wardens left two keys because they lacked courage to lock the door from inside. Order freezes; Ember consumes.'

choices.label: Ask how to survive the Threshold's choice.

text: 'Your mercy steadied a blind man's conscience. Take my blessing—may your mind stay clear when the seals fracture.'
'Turn those lead cylinders to clean ash, and I will teach your casters how to ground the Anchor Seals without losing their sanity.'
'I wrote the equations that opened the first cinder-gates. All the ash falling across four provinces began as ink on my desk.'
'The First Watch awaits its discharge, and the seals tremble. Walk into the nave with an unclouded heart.'
